subject: general
question: The Garuda pillar at Besnagar was erected by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Heliodorus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Garuda pillar at Besnagar**, also known as the **Heliodorus Pillar**, is one of the earliest known examples of an Indian pillar erected by a foreigner.
 
• It was erected by **Heliodorus**, a Greek ambassador from the court of **Antialcidas**, the Indo-Greek king of Taxila, around the **2nd century BCE**.
 
• The pillar was dedicated to **Vasudeva (Vishnu)**, showcasing the influence of Vaishnavism during that period.
 
• Heliodorus inscribed the pillar with a dedication, in Brahmi script, which explains that he was a devotee of Vasudeva and commissioned the pillar to honor him.
 
• This pillar is located in **Vidisha (Besnagar)**, Madhya Pradesh, and is a significant archaeological site for understanding the cultural and religious exchange between Greeks and Indians during ancient times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heliodorus and His Significance:**

 
 
• Heliodorus was a Greek ambassador sent by Antialcidas, a ruler of the Indo-Greek kingdom, to the court of the Shunga king **Bhagabhadra**.
 
• The inscription on the Garuda pillar is one of the earliest records of a foreigner adopting Indian religious practices, specifically Vaishnavism.
 
• The pillar inscription refers to Heliodorus as a **Bhagavata**, indicating his devotion to Vasudeva (an early form of Vishnu).
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features of the Garuda Pillar:**
 
 
• The pillar is topped with a **Garuda**, the mythical bird and vehicle of Vishnu, symbolizing the deity's presence.
 
• It is made of sandstone and stands approximately **6.7 meters** tall.
 
• The pillar inscription is written in Brahmi script and Prakrit language, emphasizing its historical and linguistic importance.
 
 
 
• **Influence of Indo-Greek Culture:**
 
 
• The erection of the Garuda pillar symbolizes the cultural and religious interactions between the Greeks and Indians during the Indo-Greek period.
 
• It highlights the spread and acceptance of Indian religions, particularly Vaishnavism, beyond its native followers.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explanation:**
 
 
• **Menander:** Menander I (Milinda) was an Indo-Greek king known for embracing Buddhism, not Vaishnavism. He is associated with the Buddhist text **Milinda Panha**.
 
• **Pushyamitra Sunga:** Pushyamitra Sunga was the founder of the Sunga dynasty, known for his patronage of Hinduism, but he had no connection to the Garuda pillar.
 
• **Kanishka:** Kanishka, the Kushan emperor, was a prominent patron of Buddhism and had no link to the Garuda pillar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Garuda pillar** is a testimony to the early spread of **Vaishnavism** and its acceptance by people from different cultures.
 
• This inscription is one of the **earliest known inscriptions** in India that confirms the worship of Vasudeva as a supreme deity.
 
• The pillar serves as an example of the fusion of **Greek and Indian cultures**, particularly during the Indo-Greek period in Indian history.
 
• It provides valuable insights into the religious and diplomatic relations during the **2nd century BCE**.
